practice.intro: Short quizzes on public nuclear topics. Check your understanding with an explanation after every question.
practice.privacy: Practice scores stay in this browser. Nothing is sent to your manager or recorded on your transcript.
practice.secure: Qualifying exams use a separate secure bank that is never shown here. Practice questions cover public, educational content only.

jpm.noRecord: No evaluation recorded for this candidate yet.
jpm.notesHint: Observed behaviour only. Never record plant-security detail.
jpm.offlineHint: Evaluations are queued on this device and synced when you reconnect.

jpm.queuedBody: They are stored on this device only until synced.
jpm.signoffBody: You confirm {name} performed this task to standard. Your sign-off is recorded in the audit log.

items.intro: Secure exam items with metadata, versions and separation of duties: one person writes, another reviews, a training manager approves.

items.optionsRequired: At least two options and a key are required.
items.referenceHint: Training material reference, for example a lesson plan code. No procedure text.
items.security: Secure item text and keys are never exported, logged or sent to the assistant. Exports contain metadata only.
items.versionNote: The new version returns to draft and must be reviewed and approved again. Earlier versions stay in the history.
items.submitBody: Another instructor reviews the item. You cannot edit it while it is in review.
items.reviewBody: You confirm the item is technically correct and the key is right. A training manager then approves it.
items.approveBody: The item can be drawn into secure exam forms.
items.retireBody: The item is no longer drawn into new exam forms. Past attempts keep their scoring.

exams.analysisNote: p is the share of candidates answering correctly; D compares the top and bottom 27%. Item text is never shown here.
exams.appealsReadOnly: Only a training manager who did not proctor or release the attempt can decide an appeal.
exams.approveFormBody: The form can then be scheduled for candidates.
exams.intro: Assemble exam forms from blueprints, schedule candidates, proctor attempts, release results, analyse items and decide appeals.
exams.noAttempts: No graded attempts for this exam yet.
exams.pickForm: Pick an exam to see its retake rules.
exams.releaseBody: {name} will see {score} ({result}). A pass issues the qualification evidence and certificate.
exams.rejectedBody: The score stands. The candidate sees your note.
exams.retireFormBody: It can no longer be scheduled. Past attempts are kept.

exams.scheduleBody: {name} is scheduled for {exam} on {when}. The exam opens on the day.

exams.signoffBody: Scores are computed automatically, but no result reaches the candidate until a proctor other than the candidate releases it.
exams.toReleaseSub: Graded, not yet visible to the candidate
exams.upheldBody: {n} items are voided and the attempt is rescored. If it now passes, the qualification evidence is issued.
exams.voidHint: Voided items are removed from the score for this attempt only.

ad.intro: Short adaptive checks for future skills. Each item adapts to your last answers, and the check stops as soon as your estimate is stable, never after more than 20 items.
ad.none: Future-skills assessments are for ENEC staff.

levelText.0: Not yet at foundation level: the items at level 1 were not answered right twice. A short course is the best next step.
levelText.1: Foundation: you know the basics and can follow guidance.
levelText.2: Working: you apply this in everyday work.
levelText.3: Proficient: you handle unusual cases and help others.
levelText.4: Expert: you handle the hardest items reliably. Evidence above level 3 comes from work, not from a check.

ad.pctSuppressedLong: A comparison with colleagues appears once 10 or more people have taken this bank.
ad.notTaken: You have not taken this assessment yet.
ad.enecSuppressed: The ENEC line appears once 10 or more people have taken this bank.

how.title: How the adaptive check works
how.body: You start at level 2. After two right answers in a row the next item is one level harder; after a wrong answer it is one level easier. Your estimate is the highest level you answered right at least twice. The check stops when the estimate has not changed over four answers (after at least eight items), or at 20 items. Safety-related skills say only whether you meet the standard.
how.engine: Deterministic rule; no AI model is used.

hist.title: My results
hist.intro: Every completed attempt, with the integrity status where the bank counts towards a credential.
hist.noneBody: Start a bank above. Your result becomes evidence in your skills passport.

privacy.title: Who sees your results
privacy.body: You see your own results. Your line manager and assessors see results for people in their scope, as they see your skill states. HR sees only aggregates, suppressed under 10 people.

stop.stable: The estimate did not change over the last {window} answers, so the check stopped after {n} items.
stop.max: The check reached its limit of {max} items.
stop.exhausted: The bank had no unused item left after {n} items.

reason.noPercentile: Criterion-referenced bank: no percentile is shown.
reason.noPercentileSafety: Safety-related skill: the result is the standard met or not; no percentile is ever shown.
reason.percentile: Higher than {pct}% of {n} colleagues (their latest results).
reason.pctSuppressed: No percentile yet: fewer than {min} colleagues have taken this bank.
reason.cap: Evidence is capped at level {level}; higher levels need work evidence.

take.intro: Answer one item at a time. The answer key stays on the server; you see your result at the end.
take.noKey: Answers are checked on the server; the next item depends on them.
take.error: The step did not go through
take.doneBody: Your result from {n} items is below. It has been added to your skills passport.
take.r1: Up to {max} items; it stops when your estimate is stable for {w} answers after at least {min} items.
take.r2: Items start at level 2 and adapt: two right answers in a row move you up, a wrong answer moves you down.
take.r3c: Safety-related: your result says whether you meet the standard (level {cut}), never a percentile.
take.r3n: Developmental: you see how you compare with colleagues once 10 or more have taken it.
take.r4: Evidence goes to your skills at up to level {cap}; you can retake after {days} days.
take.gatingNote: This bank counts towards a credential, so the attempt carries an integrity report (time per item, repeats, exposure).

res.title: Your result
res.intro: The level estimate, the comparison line, the path the check took and the evidence it wrote.
res.noEvidence: No evidence: the estimate is below level 1.
res.evidenceNote: Your latest attempt on this bank replaces the evidence of earlier ones.
res.criterionNote: Safety-related skills are criterion-referenced: you meet the standard or not. No ranking is ever shown.
res.voidedBody: An assessor voided this attempt after reviewing its integrity report, so it does not count and its evidence was withdrawn. You can take it again.

pt.intro: Scenario tasks on simulated plant data: find the anomaly, decide what to do and justify it. An assessor scores your answer against a rubric you see before you start.
pt.taskIntro: Read the rubric first, then work the scenario.
pt.noPlant: Synthetic trend set; no plant, OT or simulator connection.

how.title: How performance tasks work
how.body: Each task gives you a short brief and a simulated trend set. Mark the signal and the reading where the anomaly shows, choose a decision, tick the checks you made and justify your decision. Two rubric lines are scored from a key; an assessor scores the other two. An unsafe decision fails the task whatever the total.

synthetic.title: Synthetic data only
synthetic.body: Every trend set is simulated for training. Kafa'a has no connection to the plant, its operational technology or a simulator.

pt.gatingNote: This task counts towards a credential, so your attempt carries an integrity report (time on task, resubmissions, retakes).
pt.passRule: Pass: {pct}% of the {max} points or more, and the critical line not at 0.
pt.rubricSeen: I have read every line of the rubric
pt.dataPreview: The data you will work with

work.title: Your answer
work.intro: Click a chart (or use the controls) to mark where the anomaly shows.
work.waitBody: You can still replace your answer until it is scored; each replacement is recorded.
work.dataEyebrow: Click a chart to mark a reading
work.submitConsequence: Your answer goes to an assessor. You can replace it until it is scored; replacements are recorded in the integrity report.
work.replaceConsequence: Your previous answer is replaced. The replacement is counted and shown to the assessor.

res.title: Scored result
res.noEvidence: No evidence: the task was not passed.
res.voidedBody: An assessor voided this attempt after reviewing its integrity report; its evidence was withdrawn.

reason.total: {total} of {max} points; the pass mark is {pass}%.
reason.critical: The decision line is critical and scored 0, so the task is not passed.

tr.intro: Results per bank, calibration and exposure of every item, and the item editor. Aggregates under 10 people are suppressed.
tr.none: Adaptive bank statistics are for training staff.
tr.suppressedBody: Results appear once {min} or more people have taken this bank.
tr.cellsSuppressed: Levels with fewer than {min} people show as 0 (suppressed).
tr.lowNote: Compared with the share of adults at level 1 or below in the OECD Survey of Adult Skills. Different scales: a reference line, not a like-for-like comparison.
tr.criterionNote: Safety-related bank: only the share meeting the standard is reported, never a ranking.

items.note: Pilot p-values are simulated; observed values appear once an item has 10 answers. Drift: more than 0.25 apart.
items.readOnly: Instructors see the banks and their calibration; only the training manager edits items.

att.intro: Attempts of people in your scope (and your own). The training manager sees all.

eng.title: The adaptive rule
eng.e1: Every item is calibrated by difficulty from 1.00 to 4.99; its whole part is the level it is served at.
eng.e2: The staircase starts at level 2, moves up after two right answers in a row and down after one wrong answer (FS01 assess engine).
eng.e3: At each level the item comes from the facet used least so far, closest to the middle of the level; the form fixed at the start rotates first items between people.
eng.e4: The estimate is the highest level answered right at least twice. The check stops when it has not changed over four answers after at least eight items, or at 20 items.
eng.e5: Safety-related banks report only whether the standard is met. Developmental banks show a percentile against 10 or more colleagues.
eng.e6: The result writes assessment evidence (capped at level 3) to the F01 skills passport; the latest attempt on a bank replaces earlier evidence.
eng.model: Deterministic and explainable: the same answers always give the same items and result, in the browser and in the database. The model slot stays disabled.

ed.optHint: 3 or 4 options, the same order in both languages
ed.rules: Items never touch plant security or exam content and never copy a secure-bank question. Each bank level keeps at least two active items. Every save is versioned and audited.

as.intro: Submitted performance tasks waiting for scoring, and the scores given. Two rubric lines come from the key; you score the other two.

rules.title: Scoring rules
rules.body: Score only what the answer shows, using the published descriptors. You cannot score your own attempt. An unsafe decision (critical line at 0) fails the task whatever the total. Every score is audited and recorded in the NEXUS ledger.

as.keyNote: Shaded: the anomaly window from the key (assessors only).
as.autoNote: Lines from the key are already scored
as.selfNote: Your own attempt: another assessor must score it.
as.confirmBody: The attempt is scored {total} of {max}. A pass writes assessment evidence to the learner's skills.

ir.title: Integrity report
ir.eyebrow: For attempts that count towards a credential
ir.intro: Every attempt that counts towards a credential carries an integrity report. Flags ask for a human look; they are not findings.
ir.pending: The report appears when the attempt is complete.
ir.notGating: This bank does not count towards a credential, so no report is kept.

flagHelp.fast_answers: three or more answers in under 5 seconds
flagHelp.short_time: under 15 seconds per item, or under the task's minimum time
flagHelp.retakes: two or more earlier attempts in the 30 days before
flagHelp.resubmissions: the answer was replaced two or more times before scoring
flagHelp.exposure: more than half the items were ones the person had already seen (tasks: 20 or more people saw the scenario before)

ir.readOnly: You can read and export every report. Assessors decide flagged reports.
ir.acceptConsequence: The attempt keeps counting. Your reason is recorded with the report.
ir.voidConsequence: The attempt stops counting and its evidence is withdrawn from the learner's skills. The learner may take it again.
ir.what: A record of how the attempt was taken, kept for attempts that count towards a credential. It never decides on its own: an assessor reviews flagged reports and records the decision.
ir.missing: This attempt counts towards a credential but has no integrity report; scoring is refused until it has one.
